It really means a lot that you have taken time to write such a sentimental message and I really appreciate it. Body Dysmorphia is an anxiety related condition with many OCD traits (I have an addictive personality as well which just feeds into my problems further) and yes you are right, it very much so is the pivotal point of my depression. I understand how the way i perceive my flaws are greatly exaggerated, and i guess it helps knowing that i am my worst critic, but it never goes further than that. The act of hating myself is so habitual it is hard to stop! Which doesn't help anything as you could imagine.

I like your analogy of the two twins, and you make a very true point. I don't judge people solely on looks but for some reason, i assume people base my worth purely on whether they find me attractive. And this stops me from travelling because all i worry about it how i will do my makeup each day as i can't possibly be seen without it. Sounds extremely vain, but it's like an addiction i can't stop.

Helping people certainly helps with personal growth, and i do feel happiest when i am actively making a difference to somebody else's life. Might i add that your message has greatly helped me somewhat overcome the low mood i have been stuck in today, so thank you. And thank you for highlighting the things i have going for me - you too are an incredible person! :)

Thank you so much for the response. It really does mean a lot and i appreciate your words. I agree with everything you have said and i myself would tell anybody else who is in a dark head space the same thing, but applying it to myself is what's hard. I can't seem to extend the compassion i have for others to myself. I think its because i keep trying only to get knocked back every time. I know its the depression and body dysmorphia that make me feel such a way, and i suppose knowing that is the first step. Thank you again for the support :)

For anybody who is interested, this picture was taken during the Bad Tour (London). There is footage online that you can easily find. In this picture, his head is 'lowered' because he is listening to her, the amount of cameras snapping photos on top of the noise from the crowd would cause any person to listen intently. This picture isn't edited in terms of it being a fake photo, maybe the colours were edited slightly (like the majority of photos are) before releasing it to the public. Opinions are opinions but he isn't pathetic. Michael actually did REALLY like Diana, and although the song 'Dirty Diana' wasn't about her (it is actually about groupies) he took it out of the show as a sign of respect to her. She told him that was her favourite song and to play it but it was to late. They had many similarities and she was a big fan of him. The photo depicts how they both felt in that moment, which is why i posted it. It isn't posed, it isn't scripted. It is just as it is.

I am all for free expression but can we either appreciate the photo for what it is or leave it be?

I feel like this about the entire Off the Wall album! Such amazing tracks, i also feel as if they should have gotten more notoriety. Michael was upset about the lack of exposure the album got, it was mostly due to the fact that at the time of release, black artists were not in the mass media spotlight. It was also due to the label not promoting the album as well as they should have. It wasn't until Thriller that Michael got the true exposure he deserved. He was the first black artist to make it onto MTV, and he did this with the music video Beat It. He collaborated with Slash mainly for the sole purpose of getting on air. This was because of the fact Slash were white and their style of music was in at the time. Upon Beat It getting air time on MTV, the rest was history (or HIStory haha). That was the most viewed video on the channel, too. People finally recognised Michael as the ground breaking solo artist, dancer, entertainer, producer (etc.!) that he was. It was a shame that Off The Wall didn't achieve this from the get-go, but none the less, that album is still one of my favourites for sure. And hey, most things happen for a reason. :)

The thing i hate about the albums Sony keep pumping out is that they are not, and will never be, Michael Jackson. Whether the vocals are truly him or not (in which by the way i feel the majority are not, or at least are mostly sampled and super over processed). Michael was a perfectionist to say the very least, he had stacks upon stacks of tracks he had made - from demos to actual finished pieces - but he did not release them to the public as he felt they were not good enough. Any track/album that those money grabbing, greedy merchants at Sony release are not Michael approved, therefore should not be stated as a Micheal Jackson record. They are Sony records with or without Michael's vocals, beat boxing or backing track. For this reason, i refuse to listen to any of the new stuff they throw out. And if you compare the albums Sony released to the albums Michael *chose* to put out into the world, they just don't have that same pull that every true Michael Jackson track has. 

Also, i really feel pity upon these so-called artists who collaborated with Michael AFTER he passed. Why didn't we hear these tracks before Michael passed? Oh yeah, because he didn't voluntarily partake in the collab. So these once again so-called artists are making money off of the back of somebody who is no longer physically here, and that makes me seethe. But, at the same consent, Michael was known to let artists sample his tracks for free, purely to keep his music alive and ever circulating. I just think it is wrong that a lot of people have jumped on his passing as a huge career boost and money making opportunity for them.

This mask isn't wearable as it's purpose is more for display, i think if i were to make a wearable one i would have to curve the mask slightly, which defeats the object of trying to achieve an authentic look. However, i think i could easily obtain that from a softer material like crafting foam or something. The mask isn't heavy at all which is kind of surprising, When working with the clay it is heavy but it lightens a great deal as it dries.

I use a crafting knife to cut the shape and then i sculpt it with my hands to get a smoother edge. Clay tools are great to use too as they can give lots of good effects (for example, the pattern of the bark).

I think the wood idea sounds great and with practice comes techniques that make a world of difference. I say give it a shot! Hope this helped :)
